title: Console: compact tracing + approximate cost UX — scope reduction and acceptance gates
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Reduce surface area for Console observability to ship a compact MVP that supports core developer workflows: route-level latency distributions, sampled trace detail for outliers, and an approximate per-route cost estimate. This ticket captures the finalized scope cuts, explicit acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and trade-offs for the compact MVP. Goal: ship within Q1 with predictable cost and bounded engineering effort while preserving the ability to iterate back towards richer drilldowns.
motivation: Recent capacity and time constraints require focusing on what customers use to troubleshoot regressions and cost spikes. Full per-token cost aggregation and exhaustive trace preservation are expensive; we need an approach that surfaces signal with bounded storage and compute costs.
scope_included: Top-level route cards with 90th/95th latency and request volume
Cost estimate widget showing approximate cost per route (30d rolling), derived from sampled token counts and model unit prices
Trace sampling: store full traces for 1% of requests by default, plus deterministic capture of errors and high-latency outliers
Inspect modal: for sampled traces only, show span timeline, model selection, and top request headers
Trace search by route + time window (limited to 7 days in MVP)
Graceful degraded UI when detailed data unavailable with clear 'why' messaging and links to export CSVs
scope_removed_or_deferred: Complete history of traces beyond 7 days (deferred)
Per-span attribution to exact model kernel selection (deferred)
Realtime per-token streaming cost meter on the console (deferred)
Deep drilldowns: per-customer multi-route comparisons in first release
tradeoffs_and_risks: Approximate cost can diverge from true invoiced amount; documented margin expected (~5-12%) depending on quantization profile
Sampling will miss some low-frequency errors; deterministic capture of errors mitigates but doesn't eliminate risk
Limited retention may frustrate customers who require forensic investigations beyond 7 days
Conservative defaults prioritize SLOs and cost over complete fidelity; marketing must align expectations
acceptance_criteria: Route cards render within 300ms for typical console sessions (measured on staging under 50 concurrent users)
Cost estimate widget displays a 30-day approximate cost per route and includes a tooltip explaining estimation method and expected error bounds
Trace sampling policy implemented: deterministic-capture of all requests with HTTP 5xx or latency > 95th percentile, plus uniform random sampling of 1% for other requests
Inspect modal loads full sampled trace within 1s for traces under 200 spans
UI shows explicit degraded messaging when requested trace data is older than retention window or not sampled
End-to-end test coverage: smoke tests for route cards, cost widget calculations, sampling policy enforcement, and inspect modal load flow
Runbook updated with steps to expand sampling and retention when customer demand justifies additional infra cost
Product docs page explaining estimation heuristics, sampling policy, and how to request extended retention is published and linked from the console
decision_log: 2025-02-11: Chose approximation + sampling over full fidelity due to infra cost constraints (decision by PM/Eng leads)
2025-02-13: Retention capped at 7 days for MVP to limit storage; plan to evaluate usage and raise to 30 days if justified
2025-02-14: Cost estimate algorithm will use sampled token counts scaled by route volume and model price list; agreed to add a conservative correction factor to reduce underestimation bias
implementation_notes: ENG will implement a low-overhead token estimator in the request path that emits lightweight telemetry for sampled and aggregated counts
Batch job computes route-level 30d rolling costs from aggregated counters; runs once per hour
Tracing pipeline will tag deterministic-captured requests with 'console_captured=true' for easier filtering
Frontend will avoid per-request expensive RPCs by fetching pre-aggregated route summaries and lazy-loading sampled traces on demand
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Scope reviewed with Design and Eng; agreed to drop per-token drilldown to meet cycle commitment
2025-02-14: ENG-19811 spike completed: prototype token estimator added in staging; accuracy within expected bounds on synthetic workloads
2025-02-16: UX mocks for compact route card and cost tooltip completed; handed to frontend for implementation
2025-02-18: End-to-end smoke tests added to CI for sampling policy; first round of flaky failures addressed
qa_plan: Synthetic load testing to validate UI latency SLOs at 50 and 200 concurrent users
Accuracy tests comparing approximate cost to full invoice on a historical dataset (script in repo)
Sampling verification: run on production shadow traffic for 48h and compare captured error rates
Manual exploratory: product + solutions will exercise inspect modal flows for several customer scenarios
rollout_plan: Canary: enable compact observability for 5% of accounts in staging first week
Production gradual rollout 10% -> 50% -> 100% across 3 days with monitoring of console errors and cost-job latency
Feature flags for sampling rate and retention to allow rollback/tuning without code changes
Communications: customer-facing release notes, in-console banner for early adopters, link to feedback form
notes_for_followups: If adoption metrics show >15% of users requesting deeper drilldowns, create follow-up ticket to evaluate increasing sampling to 5% and retention to 30 days
Investigate adding a bias-correction signal from offline invoice reconciliation to improve cost estimate accuracy over time
Coordinate with Sales for a partner path to offer extended retention as an add-on for Dedicated/Private customers
